summary: Adds an Enumerable IEJoin operator, a converter rule registered in the default Enumerable rule sets, and a linq4j IEJoinEnumerator for inner joins with two or more cross-input inequality predicates.

tests.evidence: New feature. Reviewer found the EnumerableIEJoinTest expectations hard to verify (hard-coded 600 later replaced by a nested-loop oracle) and asked what happens when both comparisons use the same field; tests for that case were added after review.

user_docs.evidence: New planner rule enabled by default, but Calcite documents Enumerable rules only through Javadoc; site/_docs has no rule catalog to update.

doc_comments.evidence: New public classes and EnumerableDefaults.ieJoin. Reviewer asked for Javadoc on IEJoinEnumerator and its fields, test helper Javadoc, a walk-through of the algorithm, generated-code comments, and flagged a copy-pasted stale comment in EnumerableIEJoin.

change_description.evidence: Title matches the Jira and the body explains the algorithm and scope; Calcite writes release notes at release time.

performance.evidence: New join algorithm chosen by cost, materializing and sorting both inputs twice (EnumerableIEJoin.computeSelfCost, IEJoinEnumerator ctor). No benchmark was provided; the reviewer asked whether IEJoin plus a residual Calc is still faster than the old join.

security.evidence: No auth, parsing of untrusted input, or escaping; materializing inputs matches existing join enumerators.

backward_compat.evidence: ENUMERABLE_IE_JOIN_RULE is added to EnumerableRules.ENUMERABLE_RULES and Programs.RULE_SET, so existing queries get new plans (CombineRelOptRulesTest.xml changes NestedLoopJoin to IEJoin).

concurrency.evidence: The enumerator opens and closes both input enumerators via try-with-resources and clears state on close; no shared state.

error_model.evidence: New IllegalArgumentException paths for unsupported conditions, key types and operators carry the offending value; the rule returns null before they can fire.

correctness.evidence: Non-trivial algorithm: tie-breaking for strict versus non-strict operators, null keys, reversed operand order, and type exclusions (floating point, unsigned). The reviewer probed double sorting and the same-field case.

user_value.evidence: New feature in the default rule set. The approving review asked why DOUBLE and other types are unsupported; the author deferred unsigned and floating-point types. linq4j API shape was also debated (InequalityOperator versus ExpressionType).

surprising_behavior.evidence: Plans change silently for existing inequality joins; results are meant to be identical, so the visible change is plan shape and memory use.

contradictions.evidence: Reviewer flagged a comment in EnumerableIEJoin that was a copy-paste not relevant to the new class; it was removed.

observability.evidence: No failure, retry or fallback paths that need logging.

spec_conformance.evidence: Must preserve SQL comparison semantics (NULL never matches, NaN and signed zero excluded by the floating-point restriction in supportsKeyTypes); handled deliberately.

plan.why: A large new algorithm plus planner integration: algorithm correctness and its cost are one focus, and API, documentation and default-rule-set impact are another.
